newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria will join open-border pact by year end.
newsitem.headline: Austria will join open-border pact by year end.

text.p: Austria is ready to lift its border controls and join the Schengen group of seven European Union countries by the end of this year, Interior Minister Karl Schloegl said on Monday.
"We are definitely ready for Schengen. A delay until the year 2000 is out of the question," he told a news conference.
As soon as France ratified the treaty, Austria would implement the agreement in November or December, he said.
But border controls with Germany will be lifted only step by step, not immediately, Schloegl said, adding that this was likely to continue until the end of 1998.
Germany has repeatedly voiced concern about Austria's ability to police its outer borders with Eastern Europe.
Schloegl dismissed the fears, saying Austria had recently made huge efforts to fulfil the necessary border control criteria.
Government heads and interior ministers from Germany, Austria and Italy will meet in mid July in Austria to clarify details regarding the lifting of border controls.

France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Portugal and Germany are full Schengen members. Greece, Italy and Austria have signed the accord but have yet to put the required legislation into place.
Austria is due on July 1 to take over the presidency of the Schengen states for six months.
